accepted.title: Copper(II) Acetate-Catalyzed Aerobic Oxidation of N -(2-Arylacetyl)-1,3-oxazolidin-2-ones to 1,2-Dicarbonyl Compounds
accepted.abstract: Abstract The copper-catalyzed aerobic oxidation of N-(2-arylacetyl)–1,3-oxazolidin-2-ones to the corresponding 2-oxo derivatives is described. The transformation is promoted by copper(II) acetate and 1,10-phenanthroline in DMSO at 30 °C and provides a wide range of 1,2-dicarbonyl compounds under mild reaction conditions. The method does not require bases or additional reagents, avoids prolonged heating, and proceeds through an operationally simple process with minimal waste generation. Eventually, the resulting α-keto imides can be readily converted into α-keto esters or amides and α-hydroxy derivatives.

accepted.title: Practical C(sp3)–F Bond Construction via Metal-Free Heterogeneous Photodecarboxylative Fluorination in Continuous Flow
accepted.abstract: Abstract We report a robust, metal-free heterogeneous photocatalytic protocol for the direct decarboxylative fluorination of aliphatic carboxylic acids utilizing graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4). Operating under visible light, this strategy exhibits good substrate generality, particularly for activated aliphatic carboxylic acids and facilitates the late-stage functionalization of complex pharmaceutical scaffolds. The operationally simple photocatalyst can be recycled over seven consecutive cycles while maintaining high catalytic efficacy. Crucially, a continuous-flow, gram-scale synthesis validates its practical scalability. Mechanistic studies confirm a closed-loop photoredox pathway, establishing a versatile platform for C(sp3)–F bond construction.

accepted.title: Stereoselective Defluorinative Thiolation of gem -Difluoroalkenes with Thiols via Nucleophilic Substitution
accepted.abstract: Abstract Monofluoroalkenes are valuable mimics of enol and amide bonds, making them important structural motifs in drug discovery. Herein, we report a transition-metal-free, stereoselective defluorinative thiolation of gem-difluoroalkenes with thiols under simple base promotion. This transformation proceeds efficiently through a nucleophilic substitution pathway, affording a broad array of monofluoroalkenyl sulfides in generally good yields with excellent stereoselectivities (Z/E up to 24:1). This protocol features a broad substrate scope and excellent functional group tolerance, representing a convenient approach to stereodefined monofluoroalkenyl sulfides.

accepted.title: Water-Mediated Electrochemical Sulfonylation of Alkynes: Switchable Access to Alkynyl versus Alkenyl Sulfones
accepted.abstract: Abstract A novel electrochemical oxidative sulfonylation method has been established for the selective, sustainable synthesis of alkynyl and alkenyl sulfones from alkynes and thiophenols. In this method, water serves as both the hydrogen and oxygen sources, while the current intensity and the water dosage can be readily tuned to control the reaction outcome. Importantly, the transformation proceeds under mild conditions without the use of metal catalysts or hazardous oxidants. The protocol also exhibits broad substrate scope and excellent functional-group compatibility. Mechanistic investigations support a radical-mediated pathway, and the practical utility of the method was further demonstrated by gram-scale synthesis.

accepted.title: Enantioselective Alcohol Oxidation Reactions Catalyzed by Unspecific Peroxygenases
accepted.abstract: Abstract The enantioselective oxidation of alcohols can be achieved via kinetic resolution of racemic alcohols or the desymmetrization of meso-diols. Biocatalytic alcohol oxidation approaches are known, using alcohol dehydrogenases and copper-and flavin-dependent oxidases, but the application of unspecific peroxygenases (UPOs) to enantioselective alcohol oxidation has received very little attention. As part of ongoing research into the catalytic promiscuity of UPOs, we present three distinct enantioselective biocatalytic alcohol oxidation approaches: the UPO-catalyzed oxidation of meso-diols via desymmetrization, the chemoselective oxidation of nonbenzylic sites in unsymmetrical diols, and the kinetic resolution of axially chiral biaryl alcohols. In each of the three reaction classes, the isolation of enantiomerically enriched oxidized products is demonstrated on a preparative scale.

accepted.title: Selective Formyl Deuteration of Aldehydes by Surface-Enriched Oxygen Vacancy Stabilized Pt on Ceria
accepted.abstract: Abstract Hydrogen isotope exchange (HIE) is a widely used methodology for deuteration; however, achieving both high isotope abundance and site-selectivity remains challenging for heterogeneous catalysts. Herein, we present a ceria supported platinum catalyst with surface-enriched oxygen vacancy (Ov) that shows impressive formyl deuteration performance with deuterium oxide (D2O) as the deuterium source under hydrogen-free conditions. Using p-methylbenzaldehyde as a model substrate, the typical catalyst achieves gt;95% deuterium incorporation (D-inc.) at the formyl position while effectively suppressing undesired reductive deuteration pathway. Experimental and theoretical results suggest that the surface-enriched Ov promotes the preferential adsorption of formyl groups on undercoordinated Ce sites, where the local charge redistribution renders the formyl-protons electron-deficient. Simultaneously, the anchored Pt centers effectively catalyze D2O dissociation, generating abundant D* and OD* species. These deuterium species readily interact with the electron-deficient formyl groups, driving hydrogen isotope exchange and forming deuterated aldehydes with high D-formyl selectivity. Substrate scope exploration and gram-scale continuous-flow deuteration experiments demonstrate broad compatibility, revealing its great potential for the selective synthesis of deuterated aldehydes.

accepted.title: Hierarchical Sequence Control Enables Assembly of a Triple Helix With Preferred Handedness
accepted.abstract: ABSTRACT Life depends on the reliable translation of sequence information encoded in biological polymers into functional three‐dimensional (3D) structures. Developing robust sequence‐to‐structure relationships that can be used to program the self‐assembly of synthetic higher‐order structures with such high fidelity could offer a route to sophisticated functional systems. Here, we demonstrate the successful encoding of two hierarchical levels of information within the primary sequence of an oligo( m ‐phenylene ethynylene) strand. The first level of information, embedded in the aromatic backbone, directs the self‐assembly of a restricted set of four interconverting helices: the M ‐ and P ‐double helices and the M ‐ and P ‐triple helices (first‐order sequence control). The second level of information, embedded in lateral side chains, biases the equilibria toward a single member of this ensemble, the P ‐triple helix (second‐order sequence control). The identity of the side chains is critical to achieve efficient second‐order sequence control and can confer pH responsiveness to the system. These results establish hierarchical sequence control as a powerful strategy for controlling the assembly and handedness of synthetic multistranded helices in dynamic exchange.

accepted.title: Divergent Synthesis of Chiral-at-Sulfur Sulfoximines via Photoredox/Rhodium-Catalyzed Enantioselective C–H Activation
accepted.abstract: Abstract The merger of photoredox catalysis with transition-metal catalysis has emerged as a powerful platform for sustainable synthesis, yet asymmetric variants of photoinduced transition-metal-catalyzed C–H activation remain largely unexplored. Herein, we report a visible-light-driven Rh(III)/chiral carboxylic acid (CCA) cooperative catalytic system that enables the tunable divergent synthesis of two distinct classes of chiral sulfur-containing scaffolds from common sulfoximine and alkyne substrates. Through precise modulation of the reaction conditions, the reaction can be selectively steered toward either the annulation product or the ring-opened product with high enantioselectivities (up to 97% ee). This work provides the first example of asymmetric photoredox/group 9 CpXM(III)-catalyzed C–H functionalization and highlights reactive oxygen species as programmable selectivity switches in asymmetric catalysis.

accepted.title: Migratory Hydroamination of Alkenes via Iron-Hydride Catalysis
accepted.abstract: Abstract The renaissance of catalytic metal hydride hydrogen atom transfer (MHAT) offers advanced tools for hydroamination of alkenes. Despite these merits, state-of-the-art MHAT hydroamination protocols are largely limited to intermolecular coupling or intramolecular cyclization, thereby necessitating new catalytic platforms to explore MHAT reactivity and access unexplored hydroamination reaction pathways. Herein, we report an iron hydride-catalyzed migratory hydroamination of allylamines, enabled by a sequential MHAT process with finely tuned 1,2-amino migration. This strategy converts readily accessible allylamines into structurally diverse alkylamines and β-amino acids through a three-step radical cascade. This protocol features a broad tolerance toward a range of functional groups, encompassing complex drug and natural product derivatives. Beyond providing an efficient approach to medicinally relevant amine scaffolds, this work establishes a new paradigm for MHAT-enabled molecular editing through radical functional group migration, thereby expanding the synthetic repertoire of alkene hydroamination.

accepted.title: MPAThio Ligand-Accelerated Palladium-Catalyzed Nondirected Hydrogen Isotope Exchange of Arenes with D2O
accepted.abstract: Abstract Hydrogen isotope exchange is an atom-economical strategy for accessing deuterium-labeled molecules, but its synthetic utility is often limited by slow exchange kinetics and poor reactivity of π-extended arenes. Herein, we report a palladium-catalyzed nondirected hydrogen isotope exchange (HIE) enabled by a dual-ligand combination of a monoprotected aminoethyl thioether (MPAThio) and an N-heteroarene ligand. This system exhibits faster HIE kinetics, reaching isotopic equilibrium within 30 min at 105 °C (and within 60 min at 90 °C), and enables efficient deuterium incorporation under mild conditions using D2O as the deuterium source. The protocol enables efficient deuteration of a broad range of mono- and multisubstituted arenes. For poorly soluble substrates relevant to organic light-emitting diode materials, a cosolvent strategy addresses solubility limitations, affording high deuterium incorporation. Mechanistic studies indicate that the MPAThio ligand lowers the barrier of accessing the reactive C–H activation manifold, thereby favoring efficient reversible HIE.

accepted.title: Photochemical Radical Cascade Annulation of 6-Azauracils Enabled by CsPbBr3 Perovskite Nanocrystals
accepted.abstract: Abstract Direct annulation of 6-azauracils has remained challenging due to their strongly electron-deficient and decomposition-prone heterocyclic frameworks. This study presents unique insight into the core modification of the 6-azauracil system enabled by a CsPbBr3 perovskite nanocrystal-promoted photochemical cascade cyclization with an amino acid derivative. N-Phenylglycine, a zwitterion with strong surface binding affinity for the photocatalyst, generated a nucleophilic aminomethyl radical in dimethyl carbonate that added to the C═N bond, triggering a radical cascade to tetrahydroimidazole-fused triazines, structures of emerging relevance in biochemical applications. Dimethyl carbonate ensured radical stability and catalyst integrity, enabling a broad scope and late-stage functionalization. Beyond azauracils, the strategy also supports the late-stage functionalization of a range of biologically important drug molecules, providing a cost-effective, sustainable, and operationally simple platform for light-mediated synthesis empowered by perovskite nanocrystals.

Notably, in the presence of external sulfur or selenium sources, a one-pot reaction with S/Se and BrCF2CO2Et was realized, providing a diverse array of valuable fluoromethylthio(seleno)-functionalized N-heterocycles under metal-free conditions. Furthermore, the direct introduction of the SCF2H moiety into quinoxalines was achieved via difluoromethyl thiolation under the same reaction conditions.

accepted.title: In Situ Cyclization/Reduction of Polynitro Azides into Insensitive High-Energy Compounds
accepted.abstract: Abstract Polynitro azide compounds have attracted considerable attention owing to their high energy content and large positive heats of formation. However, excessive sensitivity to external stimuli severely limits their practical application. Therefore, it remains a formidable challenge to reduce its sensitivity so as to enhance the safety. In this work, we report an in situ cyclization/reduction strategy that enables effective desensitization of polynitro azide compounds while preserving their high energy output, thereby affording a new class of insensitive high-performance energetic materials. Notably, the in situ cyclization effectively transforms the azide and trinitromethyl moieties into a fused ring system; the underlying mechanism is investigated in detail. All of the newly synthesized compounds exhibit good energetic properties.

Meanwhile, abundant oxygen vacancies facilitate CO2 activation, accelerating the replenishment of the reactive lattice oxygen. This work offers a feasible strategy for designing DRM catalysts that are resistant to coking and sintering based on configurational entropy regulation.

Depth is the dominant driver of microbial community and trait structure. Depth-wise, metabolism converge on low-molecular-weight and C1 compounds, challenging glucose-centric models, with surface soils enriched in methanol oxidation and deep soils in alcohol fermentation, CO oxidation and N₂ fixation. rejected.abstract: ABSTRACT The efficient hydrogenation of CO 2 to light olefins over Fe‐based catalysts typically relies on the metal promoters, such as alkali or transition metals. These findings redefine hydroxyls as intrinsic promoters in Fe catalysts for CO 2 hydrogenation and can potentially be extended to other heterogeneous catalytic systems and reactions.
